pigmentSpectrum.title: What colour should a leaf be?
pigmentSpectrum.subtitle: Pick a sky, then drag the band of light the pigments absorb
pigmentSpectrum.plotLabel: Arriving light across wavelength, with the absorbed band marked
pigmentSpectrum.peakNote: Where this sky delivers most photons
pigmentSpectrum.capturedNote: Share of arriving photons the band takes in
pigmentSpectrum.leafColorNote: The light left over is the colour you see
pigmentSpectrum.hint: A leaf is the colour of the light it declines to absorb. Earth's chlorophyll takes in blue and red and lets the green in between bounce back out — which is why our forests are green, and it is an inherited quirk rather than a law of physics. Set the sky to our Sun and park the band on blue and red to watch that green fall out. Then switch to both of Pandora's suns: the cooler orange companion floods the long wavelengths, so a band stretched from green into the near-infrared harvests far more light — and the leftovers come back blue and violet.

stomatalBargain.title: The trade at the pore
stomatalBargain.subtitle: Open the pore to feed, and water leaves through the same gap
stomatalBargain.poreLabel: A leaf pore in cross-section, with carbon entering and water leaving
stomatalBargain.verdictSaturated: The leaf is full: carbon arrives faster than the enzymes can spend it, so opening the pore any further buys nothing and costs water.
stomatalBargain.verdictHungry: The leaf is still hungry. Carbon is the limit here, so it must hold the pore open — and pay in water for every molecule it gets.
stomatalBargain.hint: There is only one door, and both gases use it. Carbon dioxide has to come in for the leaf to eat, and water vapour goes out through the same gap — no plant has ever found a way to open one direction only. In Earth's air, carbon is so scarce that a leaf must hold the pore wide and bleed water to feed itself at all. Push the air toward Pandora's carbon-thick mixture and the arithmetic inverts: the gradient does the work, a barely-cracked pore feeds the whole leaf, and the water bill nearly disappears. Watch the last readout too — a leaf grows fewer pores in richer air, which is why counting pores on a fossil leaf tells you what its sky was made of.

rubiscoLedger.title: A hundred turns of one enzyme
rubiscoLedger.subtitle: Teal caught carbon and made sugar; magenta caught oxygen by mistake
rubiscoLedger.gridLabel: One hundred enzyme turns, {mistakes} of them mistakes
rubiscoLedger.pumpRedundant: buying nothing — the air is already rich
rubiscoLedger.pumpEarning: earning its keep in thin air
rubiscoLedger.verdictRedundant: The pump is now dead weight. It spends extra energy to concentrate carbon the atmosphere already delivers for free — which is why a carbon-thick world would never evolve one.
rubiscoLedger.verdictClean: Almost no mistakes left. With this much carbon at the enzyme, oxygen barely gets a turn and nothing has to be cleaned up.
rubiscoLedger.verdictLeaky: The enzyme keeps grabbing the wrong gas, and every mistake costs energy to undo and hands some hard-won carbon straight back.
rubiscoLedger.hint: The enzyme that feeds nearly every food chain on Earth cannot reliably tell carbon dioxide from oxygen. Catch carbon and you get sugar; catch oxygen and you get a broken fragment the cell must spend energy to salvage, giving some carbon back in the process. Earth's leaves live with this because carbon dioxide dissolves far better in water than oxygen does — otherwise the error rate would be ruinous. Slide the air toward Pandora's mixture and the magenta drains out of the grid entirely. Then try the pumped strategies: they are worth their extra energy in thin air and worthless the moment the air itself is rich.

sugarFreight.title: Shipping sugar down a trunk
sugarFreight.subtitle: No pump — just pressure at the top, and a very long pipe
sugarFreight.trunkLabel: Sugar parcels descending a trunk from canopy to root
sugarFreight.gradientNote: MPa along each metre of trunk
sugarFreight.verdictWorkable: A workable freight line: sugar reaches the roots while it is still needed there.
sugarFreight.verdictSlow: This shipment now takes weeks. A tree this tall cannot run on pressure alone unless its plumbing is nothing like ours.
sugarFreight.hint: Sugar goes down a tree the same way water goes up it: with no pump at all. Loading sugar into the transport pipe at a sunlit leaf pulls water in behind it and raises the pressure there; at the root, sugar is spent, water leaves, and the pressure drops. That difference shoves the whole loaded column downward. The trap is geometric — make the tree twice as tall and you double the distance while halving the push behind each metre, so travel time grows with the square of height. An Earth redwood's canopy-to-root run already takes over a week. Drag the height out to canon's tallest Hometrees and watch what happens.

arbuscular-mycorrhiza.title: Arbuscular Mycorrhiza
arbuscular-mycorrhiza.info: Fungal arbuscules branch inside root cells. Toggle the symbiosis; phosphorus inflows while carbon pays the fungus at the interface.

biome.title: Biome
biome.info: Climate wheel of temperature × precipitation. Drag the dial; the matching biome morphs — rainforest, tundra, desert, Pandoran glow-forest.

canopy.title: Canopy
canopy.info: Vertical forest slice. Drop a light-meter through the crown; intensity falls exponentially and understory plants adapt at each depth.

cohesion-tension.title: Cohesion–Tension
cohesion-tension.info: A continuous water column under tension. Pull harder at the leaves; the column rises. Overpull and a cavitation bubble snaps the stream.

common-mycorrhizal-network.title: Common Mycorrhizal Network
common-mycorrhizal-network.info: Trees share a glowing fungal web. Inject carbon at a hub tree and watch it flow underground to shaded seedlings — the wood-wide web.

cytoplasmic-streaming.title: Cytoplasmic Streaming
cytoplasmic-streaming.info: Organelles ride a looping current inside a giant cell. Raise velocity and nutrients spread fast; stall it and distribution freezes.

ectomycorrhiza.title: Ectomycorrhiza
ectomycorrhiza.info: A fungal mantle sheaths the root tip; the Hartig net runs between cells, never inside. Contrast with arbuscular type at the sheath.

emergent-layer.title: Emergent Layer
emergent-layer.info: Giants poke above the closed canopy. Scroll the forest profile upward; full sun and wind hit, and exposure meters spike at the top.

epiphyte.title: Epiphyte
epiphyte.info: A plant on a host tree with no soil and no parasitism. Place it at canopy heights; it sips water and debris from air alone.

foliage-height-diversity.title: Foliage-Height Diversity
foliage-height-diversity.info: Vertical leaf-density histogram. Redistribute foliage across heights; the diversity index rises and more animal niches open.

forest-floor.title: Forest Floor
forest-floor.info: Darkest stratum — about 2% of sunlight. Shine a lamp to reveal decomposers, fungi, and detritus; the nutrient loop closes here.

forest-stratification.title: Forest Stratification
forest-stratification.info: Five labeled vertical layers. Click a stratum to highlight light, humidity, and inhabitants — Earth cutaway or Pandoran glow variant.

hypha.title: Hypha
hypha.info: A single fungal thread grows and branches live. Steer the tip toward a nutrient patch; extension speed tracks the gradient.

leaf-area-index.title: Leaf Area Index
leaf-area-index.info: Stack leaf layers over a ground patch. LAI climbs and light interception saturates — more leaves, diminishing returns.

mother-tree-hypothesis.title: Mother Tree Hypothesis
mother-tree-hypothesis.info: A hub tree feeds seedlings through mycorrhizal links. Shade a juvenile and the mother routes more carbon its way.

mycelium.title: Mycelium
mycelium.info: An expanding fungal colony explores substrate. Drop food sources; threads reorganize toward them and prune unused paths.

mycorrhiza.title: Mycorrhiza
mycorrhiza.info: Root–fungus trade balance. Carbon from the plant vs phosphorus and nitrogen from the fungus; lean the soil and the scale tips.

seed-bank.title: Seed Bank
seed-bank.info: Dormant seeds wait at depth. Trigger fire, flood, or a light gap; the matching cohort germinates while others stay asleep.

transpiration.title: Transpiration
transpiration.info: Stomata open and vapor escapes. Tune humidity, heat, and wind; the rate gauge moves and the water column is tugged upward.

turgor-pressure.title: Turgor Pressure
turgor-pressure.info: A cell inflates or wilts with water. Shift the osmotic gradient from turgid and firm to plasmolyzed; the whole shoot droops.

understory.title: Understory
understory.info: Shaded layer beneath the crown. Open canopy gaps; light flecks shift. Shade-tolerant plants thrive while sun-plants stall.

xylem.title: Xylem
xylem.info: Vessel bundle lifting water. Widen diameter for faster Hagen–Poiseuille flow — and higher cavitation risk on the gauge.
